description: Me gusta la astronomia, buscar estrellas en el telescopio, hacer proyectos de robotica, usar la impresora 3d, leer libros de ciencia y el espacio y jugar Astroneer, Planet Crafter, Minecraft y mas.
summary: Kamo and the Machines of Mars is an interactive story, narrated by Kamo, a scientist and astronaut cat drawn by one of our team members, that keeps six machines left on Mars from being forgotten: Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance and Ingenuity. Visitors explore a perspective map of Mars, a 1997–2026 timeline, 3D models with tappable parts, two mini-games and a quiz. Each machine becomes a time capsule: what it was built for, what it found, how its mission ended and why it still matters. The project turns NASA mission data into a story that students and families can explore in English or Spanish, in any browser.
details:
What it does. Our project answers the challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten” by telling the story of the six machines humanity has left on Mars. A narrator, Kamo, guides the visitor through a short journey: a perspective map shows where each machine landed, a timeline from 1997 to 2026 shows which machines were working each year, and each machine has its own page with a hand-made drawing, its mission, its biggest discovery, how it ended and why it matters today. A short imaginary letter in each machine’s voice, clearly labeled as imaginary, adds an emotional layer.

How people explore. Visitors can rotate simplified 3D models and tap named parts to learn what they do, watch a chart of how much longer each machine worked than planned (for example, Opportunity was planned for 90 sols and worked more than 14 years; Ingenuity was planned for 5 flights and made 72), compare their sizes at real scale next to a person, and see how many kilometers each rover has driven. Two mini-games let them feel the real constraints: flying Ingenuity in Mars’s very thin air, and driving Opportunity while dust covers its solar panels. A 10-question quiz closes the journey.

Why it matters. The machines on Mars are not abandoned: they are time capsules that keep teaching us about water, climate and the possibility of life. By combining accurate NASA data with storytelling and play, the project helps young people and families connect with space exploration. It is built in Guatemala, available in English and Spanish, and runs in a web browser without installing anything.

Abandoned and still working. The challenge asks for the story of hardware that is silent or still active. Our story is centered on four machines that are no longer working (Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity), and it includes Curiosity and Perseverance as the machines that carry their work forward. Every rover page shows a clear status label (for example, “Silent since 2018” or “Still working today”), and the pages with distances and durations mark which machines are still active and give the date of the data (October 12, 2026), so the numbers are read correctly even months later.

How we built it. The page is a single web page made with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. The 3D models use the three.js library, the original music is generated in the browser with the Web Audio API, and the games use HTML canvas. The drawings are original hand-made art by a team member. We checked facts (landing dates, durations, sizes, distances) against NASA/JPL sources and note on the page when a value is approximate.
dataRefs: • NASA Science, “Mars Pathfinder” (mission page): Sojourner and its 1997 landing, planned 7 sols and 83 sols of work.
• NASA Science, “Mars Exploration Rovers: Spirit and Opportunity” (mission page): landing dates, planned and actual durations.
• NASA/JPL, Mars Exploration Rover launch press kit (June 2003): dimensions and mass of the twin rovers.
• NASA Science, “Mars Science Laboratory: Curiosity Rover” (mission page): mass, size, instruments and cameras
• NASA Science, Curiosity “Location Map”: where the rover is on Mount Sharp.
• NASA Science, Curiosity “Science Updates” (blog): sols on Mars and recent findings.
• NASA Science, “Curiosity reaches 1 kilometer of elevation gain” (August 26, 2026).
• NASA, “Curiosity celebrates 10 years on Mars”: prime mission of one Mars year (687 Earth days).
• NASA/JPL, Mars 2020 Perseverance landing press kit, mission section: prime mission of one Mars year (687 Earth days).
• NASA/JPL, Mars 2020 Perseverance launch press kit, “Perseverance Rover”: size, mass, cameras and instruments.
• NASA Science, “Ingenuity Mars Helicopter” (page): its planned 5 flights and the 72 it made.
• NASA/JPL, “How NASA’s Mars Helicopter Will Reach the Red Planet’s Surface”: Ingenuity height, body size, rotor span and mass.
• NASA/JPL news, “NASA’s Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven” (October 12, 2026).
• NASA Science, “Comparing Off-World Rover Driving Distances” (distance infographic, as of October 2026): kilometers driven by each rover.
• NASA Science, “Evolution of NASA’s Mars Rovers: Sojourner to Perseverance.”

• NASA/JPL-Caltech map of Mars landing sites, from “Cómo aterrizamos en Marte” (“How We Land on Mars”), used as the base image of our perspective map. Dot positions follow the official latitudes and longitudes of each site.
